{"id": "ea0268d7-8674-40d2-8987-3bc506e43baa", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_FZrVacNfpT1ZsslxDMyt0N", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"context\":\"## Requesting a quota increase\\n\\nThe steps for requesting a quota increase for your account depend on the value in the **Adjustable** column in the quotas table in Amazon Bedrock service quotas.\\n\\n**Important:**\\n\\nBefore requesting a quota increase, verify that the model is not in a *Legacy* or *Deprecated* lifecycle status. Quota increases are not granted for models that are scheduled for retirement. Check the model's lifecycle status on the Model lifecycle page and consider migrating to the successor model instead.\\n\\n* If a quota is marked as **Yes**, you can adjust it by following the steps at Requesting a Quota Increase in the Service Quotas User Guide.\\n* For any model, you can request an increase for the following quotas together:\\n\\n + Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`\\n + On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`\\n + Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day\\n\\n To request an increase for any combination of these quotas, request an increase for the **Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for `${model}`** quota by following the steps at Requesting a Quota Increase in the Service Quotas User Guide. After you do so, the support team will reach out and offer you the option of also increasing the other two quotas.\\n\\n **Note:**\\n\\n Due to overwhelming demand, priority will be given to customers who generate traffic that consumes their existing quota allocation. Your request might be denied if you don't meet this condition.\\n\\nFor `bedrock-mantle` quota increases, see Requesting a quota increase\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-runtime.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"How do I troubleshoot the \\\"ThrottlingException\\\" error when I use Amazon Bedrock on-demand resources?\",\"context\":\"### Request a quota increase\\n\\nNew AWS accounts might have lower initial quotas than the default quotas. Specific models have non-adjustable fixed quotas. If your workload traffic exceeds your account's on-demand quotas, then contact [AWS Support](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/case-management.html#creating-a-support-case) or your account manager to [request a quota increase](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-increase.html). AWS might adjust default quotas based on usage patterns or service requirements.\\n\\nInclude the following information in your request:\\n\\n* The name of the quota to increase\\n* Your current quota value and the quota value that you require\\n* The model ID\\n* The Region for the quota increase\\n* A brief explanation of your use case\\n* Your projected usage, including steady and peak tokens and requests per minute, and average input and output tokens per request\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/bedrock-throttling-error\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"bedrockruntime\",\"context\":\"## type ThrottlingException \\n\\n```\\ntype ThrottlingException struct {\\n RespMetadata protocol.ResponseMetadata `json:\\\"-\\\" xml:\\\"-\\\"`\\n\\n Message_ *string `locationName:\\\"message\\\" type:\\\"string\\\"`\\n // contains filtered or unexported fields\\n}\\n```\\n\\nYour request was throttled because of service-wide limitations. Resubmit\\nyour request later or in a different region. You can also purchase Provisioned\\nThroughput (<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prov-throughput.html>)\\nto increase the rate or number of tokens you can process\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-go/api/service/bedrockruntime/index.html\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"Quotas for the bedrock-mantle endpoint\",\"context\":\"## How requests are evaluated against quotas\\n\\nWhen you submit an inference request to the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint, AWS evaluates it against your quotas in the following order:\\n\\n1. **Input tokens per minute** \u2013 The number of input tokens in the request, plus the value of `max_tokens` (or the model-specific maximum if `max_tokens` is not set), is checked against the input-tokens-per-minute quota for the requested model. If admitting the request would exceed the quota, the request is throttled with an HTTP 429 response.\\n2. **Output tokens per minute** \u2013 As the model streams or generates output, output tokens are counted against the output-tokens-per-minute quota for that model. If the quota is reached during generation, generation stops and the response is returned with a finish reason indicating the cutoff.\\n\\nAfter the response completes, any unused portion of the initial input-token reservation (the difference between `max_tokens` and the actual output) is replenished to your quota.\\n\\nThe endpoint may apply additional internal rate limiting that is not exposed in Service Quotas. Use retry logic with exponential backoff to handle transient throttling.\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint's TPM quotas count input and output tokens together against a single per-model quota, while the `bedrock-mantle` endpoint applies separate input-tokens-per-minute and output-tokens-per-minute quotas. If you run workloads on both endpoints, plan capacity for each endpoint independently. For details on the runtime endpoint's quotas, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/quotas-mantle.html\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Scaling and throughput best practices\",\"context\":\"## `bedrock-runtime` endpoint: throughput and quotas\\n\\nThe `bedrock-runtime` endpoint has the following quota behavior:\\n\\n* Per-model, per-Region token quotas count input and output tokens together. Output tokens consume quota according to a model-specific burndown rate.\\n* Some models also have RPM quotas, while other models are governed only by token quotas. Check the quotas that apply to the exact model and inference profile that you use.\\n* Per-minute and per-day token quotas are shared across the inference APIs that call the same model on this endpoint. Allocations for `bedrock-runtime` and `bedrock-mantle` are independent.\\n* Custom inference profiles, batch inference, and Provisioned Throughput have separate quotas and are available only through `bedrock-runtime`.\\n\\nFor current quota values, token-burndown details, and the quota-increase process, see Quotas for the bedrock-runtime endpoint. See the applicable Models at a glance for model-specific endpoint, service-tier, and feature support\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/scaling-throughput-best-practices.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search AWS docs for Bedrock quota increase guidance"}

{"id": "927c127d-a068-4e30-8f78-873e7f930e32", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Here's how to raise the quota, plus a few things to check before you do.

## Request the increase
1. **Open Service Quotas** for Amazon Bedrock in the Region where you're being throttled. Find the quota for your exact model, for example *On-demand InvokeModel tokens per minute for <model>* or *Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens per minute for <model>*.
2. **Check the Adjustable column.** If it says **Yes**, you can request the increase from the console. If it says No, the quota is fixed for that model and can't be raised.
3. **Request the increase on the Cross-Region InvokeModel tokens-per-minute quota** for the model. This one request can also cover the on-demand tokens-per-minute and Cross-Model Max Tokens Per Day quotas. The support team contacts you afterward and offers to raise the other two.
4. **If the console route isn't available**, open an AWS Support case or contact your account manager.

Include these details in the request:
- The quota name, your current value and the value you need
- The model ID and the Region
- A short description of your use case
- Your projected steady and peak tokens per minute and requests per minute, and your average input and output tokens per request

## Things that affect approval
- **Model lifecycle:** Increases aren't granted for models in *Legacy* or *Deprecated* status. If yours is, move to the successor model.
- **Actual usage:** AWS prioritizes customers who are already consuming their existing quota, so a request can be denied if your traffic doesn't use what you have now.
- **New accounts:** These often start with lower quotas than the defaults.
- **Endpoint:** `bedrock-runtime` and `bedrock-mantle` have independent quotas. On `bedrock-runtime`, input and output tokens count together against one per-model quota, and output tokens are weighted by a model-specific burndown rate. A large `max_tokens` setting can therefore use up quota faster than you'd expect.

## Mitigations while you wait
- Add **retries with exponential backoff and jitter** for ThrottlingException.
- Lower `max_tokens` to what you actually need.
- Use a **cross-Region inference profile** to spread load across Regions.
- Consider **Provisioned Throughput** for steady, high-volume workloads. It has its own quotas and is available only through `bedrock-runtime`.

If you tell me the model ID and Region, I can look at your current quota values and recent throttling metrics. That would show whether you're hitting a tokens-per-minute or requests-per-minute limit, and how big an increase to ask for.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
